standard.title: Producing food and fibre
standard.description: describe the ways of producing food and fibre
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explore how plants and animals are grown for food, clothing and shelter (AC9TDE2K03). They have encountered food and fibre production at an exploratory level. They have not yet described production methods, compared different production systems, or examined tools and technologies used in food and fibre production.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe the ways food and fibre are produced, including tools, equipment and procedures used to support plant and animal production.

nodes.label: Methods of food production
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe at least two methods used to produce food and explain what each involves
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two food production methods (e.g. growing vegetables, raising livestock, fishing) and explain what each involves
nodes.typical_width: Describe a range of food production methods in Australia — plant-based (crops, vegetables, orchards) and animal-based (livestock, dairy, seafood); explain what tools, equipment and procedures are involved in each
wider: Research food and fibre production techniques developed by First Nations Australians — including burning, tilling, planting, transplanting, watering, weeding, thinning, cropping, storing and trading — and describe how these methods support sustainable production
Compare farming methods for food in Australia and a country in Asia — describe how different plants and animals are used and how diverse technologies support their production
success_criteria: Names at least two food production methods
Describes what is involved in at least one method (tools, procedures, environment)

nodes.label: Methods of fibre production
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how animal and plant fibres are produced and name examples of each
nodes.minimum_width: Name one animal fibre and one plant fibre and describe how each is produced
nodes.typical_width: Describe how animal fibres (wool, alpaca) and plant fibres (timber, cotton, bamboo) are produced in Australia; explain what tools, equipment and production environments are involved; compare at least two fibre types
wider: Research how production of plantation timbers differs from bamboo production — compare growth rates, land use, harvesting methods and sustainability implications
Investigate how First Nations Australians produced and used plant and animal fibres — describe production methods and how they differ from contemporary industrial fibre production

response_modes.reason: Students often know that wool comes from sheep but have thin understanding of the production process — shearing, processing, spinning. Fibre types vary significantly in production method, and examining both animal and plant fibres prevents students from over-generalising from one example.

success_criteria: Names at least one animal fibre and one plant fibre correctly
Describes the production process for at least one fibre type

nodes.label: Tools, environments and production systems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how tools, equipment and production environments (e.g. school garden, glasshouse, animal housing) are used to improve food or fibre production
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one production environment (e.g. a school garden, a glasshouse, a chicken shelter) and explain how it improves production
nodes.typical_width: Describe how different tools, equipment and production environments support plant and animal production; explain how each improves yield, safety or sustainability; include examples from both plant-based and animal-based production
wider: Design and describe a simple production environment (e.g. a school vegetable garden, a seed propagation setup) — identify what tools and procedures would improve production and justify choices
Investigate how protected cropping (glasshouses) changes what can be produced and where — compare to outdoor farming and discuss what factors influence the choice of production environment

response_modes.reason: Describing production systems integrates knowledge of methods (node 1 and 2) with the tools and environments that make those methods effective. Students who understand methods separately often do not connect them to the infrastructure that supports production — this node is where that integration happens.

success_criteria: Names at least one production environment and explains its purpose
Connects tools or equipment to a specific production improvement
